title: Multi-class: one-vs-rest & softmax
intro: More than two classes? scikit-learn handles it automatically: separate binary classifiers per class (one-vs-rest) or one joint model with softmax.
keyPoints: Multi-class = 3+ classes. Two strategies: one-vs-rest and multinomial (softmax).
OvR: one binary classifier per class ('this class or not'); highest score wins.
Softmax: one joint model; k scores → a probability distribution summing to 1.
Both strategies give coefficients with one row per class.

blocks.html: Multi-class = 3 or more classes. Two strategies do the work.
One-vs-rest: one binary classifier per class (“class 0 or not-0?”). Predicting: all classifiers compute their raw output — the largest wins.

blocks.caption: Rebuilding one-vs-rest by hand
blocks.source:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

X, y = load_wine(return_X_y=True)

# Three binary classifiers: 'class 0 or not', 'class 1 or not', ...
clfs = [LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000).fit(X, y == c) for c in (0, 1, 2)]

i = 0
raw = [clf.decision_function([X[i]])[0] for clf in clfs]
print('Raw outputs per classifier:', np.round(raw, 2))
print('Manual OvR prediction     :', int(np.argmax(raw)),
      '(largest raw output)')

blocks.html: What makes OvR attractive: you simply reuse your existing binary classifier implementation — nothing new is needed. scikit-learn does this, among others, via the liblinear solver.
Multinomial adapts the loss (softmax / cross-entropy) and fits once for all classes — the standard in neural networks.

blocks.label: softmax
blocks.latex: \hat{p}_k \;=\; \frac{e^{z_k}}{\sum_{j=1}^{K} e^{z_j}}, \qquad z_k = \text{raw output for class } k
blocks.caption: The generalised sigmoid for K classes: all probabilities are positive and sum to 1.

rows: loss is closer to accuracy — sometimes a better score

sections.title: What do the coefficients look like?

blocks.html: Binary: 1 coefficient per feature. With 3 classes and 13 features (wine): coef_ is a 3×13 array — OvR gives three full classifiers, multinomial exactly as many parameters.

blocks.caption: Comparing coefficient shapes
blocks.source:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# liblinear does one-vs-rest; lbfgs (default) does multinomial
ovr = LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear', max_iter=5000).fit(X, y)
multi = LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000).fit(X, y)

print('OvR         coef_:', ovr.coef_.shape, ' intercept_:', ovr.intercept_.shape)
print('Multinomial coef_:', multi.coef_.shape, ' intercept_:', multi.intercept_.shape)
print('OvR predicts        :', ovr.predict([X[0]])[0])
print('Multinomial predicts:', multi.predict([X[0]])[0])
